title: Grassfire: does it read as a fire front now?
question: Watch the two strips step together. Does one of them read as a fire crossing a meadow — a front, flames, smoke, a burnt scar — rather than grass changing colour?
context_md:
Your standing verdict on the last grassfire card was *"The fire looks bad. Just looks like you are cycling colors. It also doesn't spread at all (if we are going to do this, moisture vs dryness should play a role."*

This is the spread-and-look half. **Same sward, same seed, same ignition** (11 cells lit at x=51). The only difference is whether burning fuel throws flames into the air. Both arms are on **bone-dry ground**, so the moisture gate is fully open in both — the wet/dry comparison is a separate card.

One arm is the behaviour that is on `main` today: with flames off and the ground dry, the ignition rule is bit-for-bit what `main` does.

**What I already measured, so you don't have to judge it by eye:** a 160-founder sward looks continuous (one empty column in a 484-column span) but is really **71 separate 4-connected islands of fuel**, and contact-only fire reaches one of them. That is the whole of "it doesn't spread at all" — the fire was not creeping, it was going out.

**What I am unsure about and want your eye on:** the *colour*. Everything that burns sits at the top of the renderer's heat ramp, and the top of that ramp is a pale yellow, so a burning meadow draws as **straw**. I have a two-constant change that makes it a strong orange, but it also moves lava, quench crust and warm water — three looks you have already judged — so it is on its own card rather than in this one.

8 frames, 45 frames apart, starting at the ignition.
